title: Who’s in and who’s out? A case study of multimodal CLIP-filtering in DataComp

bias_targets.methodology: Keyword-based search in the text modality to compute and compare filter pass rates for LGBTQ+ identity terms.

Analyzing filter pass rates through text keyword searches, evaluating gender-stereotypical word associations, and applying facial attribute imputation (via Amazon Rekognition and kNN clustering of CLIP embeddings) to compare pass rates for male and female imputed images.

Comparing filter pass rates using textual identity keyword searches and facial attribute imputation via kNN clustering of CLIP embeddings (using the Chicago Face Database as a reference) to determine exclusion rates for different racial groups.
Keyword-based search in the text modality to compute and compare filter pass rates for different religious identity terms (e.g., Muslim, Christian, Jewish).
Applying facial attribute imputation via Amazon Rekognition to estimate age groups from images and comparing their respective filter pass rates.
Using the 'langdetect' library on text samples to compute and compare filter pass rates across different detected languages, particularly contrasting Western and non-Western languages.
Analyzing source URLs using country-code top-level domains and mapping IP addresses to geolocation databases to compare filter pass rates between Western and non-Western regions.
Correlating dataset filter pass rates with textual mentions of occupations mapped to O*NET job titles, salary data, and prestige scores.
Applying a dialect prediction model to a subset of English-detected text to compute frequency and pass rates by imputed dialect.
